meta.topic: Kido Butai (Japanese carrier striking force), submarine Advance Force and the five Type A midget submarines, attack on Pearl Harbor, 7 December 1941
meta.timeConvention: Hawaii local time of 1941 (UTC-10:30) as HH:MM on 1941-12-07 unless a 'date' field is given. Tokyo time (JST, UTC+9) = Hawaii + 19h30m.
meta.positionConvention: Decimal degrees WGS84, west longitude negative. Bearings/courses in degrees true.

evidenceTags.S: seen in a search result during this research session (source listed in 'sources')
evidenceTags.M: from the researcher's knowledge of the cited literature, not re-verified in this session (direct page fetching was blocked and the shared web-search budget ran out)
evidenceTags.E: researcher's own estimate, dead reckoning or geometric reconstruction

meta.caveat: No surviving primary source that could be reached in this session gives the force's latitude/longitude on 7 December. Every Kido Butai position on 6-7 December is dead-reckoned (tag E) from the best-attested facts: launch about 220-230 nm due north of Oahu, 24 knots, due-south approach, turn to port into an ENE-E wind, and the Opana radar plot of the first wave. Treat positions as good to roughly +/-20 nm, and the screen/escort stations as schematic.
meta.crossCheck: The 06:20 force position (25.446, -157.862) matches the first-wave departure point used in research/wave1.json (25.45, -157.85) and back-projects the Opana 07:02 plot (132 statute miles, 003 deg) at about 157 kn ground speed.

ships.name: Akagi
ships.unit: 1st Air Fleet flagship / Carrier Division 1 (VAdm Nagumo Chuichi; chief of staff RAdm Kusaka Ryunosuke; air staff Cdr Genda Minoru)
ships.funnels: One large funnel on the starboard side amidships, angled outward and downward below flight-deck level (opposite the small port-side island).
ships.note: Nagumo's flagship and formation guide. Island on the PORT side amidships. Three elevators. No hinomaru on the flight deck in December 1941; white deck stripes, red-and-white striped round-down aft, katakana 'A' identification letter on the after flight deck. Flew the 'Z' signal flag and battle ensign at launch (Fuchida).

formation.basis: Guide ship. Head of the starboard (CarDiv 1) column in the reconstruction; see 'formation' object.

ships.name: Kaga
ships.funnels: One funnel on the starboard side amidships, curved outward and downward below flight-deck level; small island on the starboard side forward of it.
ships.note: Slowest carrier of the force (28 kn). Heaviest aircraft losses of the raid (15). One level bomber of the planned 15 failed to launch in the first wave; one of the planned 27 dive bombers did not go in the second.

formation.basis: E: second ship of the starboard column. A film frame taken from Akagi during the crossing shows Kaga astern of Akagi with Zuikaku beyond her (S: NHHC NH 75483 caption). Interval is a doctrinal estimate.

ships.name: Soryu
ships.unit: Carrier Division 2 (flagship of RAdm Yamaguchi Tamon)
ships.funnels: Two funnels on the starboard side amidships, both curved downward; small island on the starboard side forward.
ships.note: One of nine planned first-wave fighters did not go; one second-wave dive bomber aborted with engine trouble (S: combinedfleet TROM).

formation.basis: E: head of the port (CarDiv 2) column, abeam of Akagi. Side assignment is by analogy with the box formation the force used in 1942 (CarDiv 1 to starboard, CarDiv 2 to port).

ships.name: Hiryu
ships.funnels: Two funnels on the starboard side amidships, both curved downward (opposite the port-side island).
ships.note: Island on the PORT side amidships, like Akagi. One fighter and one dive bomber of the planned second-wave launch did not go.

formation.basis: E: second ship of the port column, astern of Soryu.

ships.name: Shokaku
ships.funnels: Two funnels on the starboard side just abaft the island, both curved downward.
ships.note: Planned first wave was 6 fighters and 27 dive bombers; one of each did not go. Fighters not used in the strikes flew combat air patrol.

formation.basis: E: rear of the port column. Which CarDiv 5 ship followed which column is inferred only from the Akagi film frame (Zuikaku behind Kaga).

ships.name: Zuikaku
ships.unit: Carrier Division 5 (flagship of RAdm Hara Chuichi)
ships.funnels: Two funnels on the starboard side just abaft the island, both curved downward.
ships.note: Planned first wave was 27 dive bombers; two did not go. LtCdr Shimazaki Shigekazu of Zuikaku led the second wave. Lost no aircraft. Flagship assignment within CarDiv 5 is M (medium).

formation.basis: E: rear of the starboard column, astern of Kaga (S: Akagi film frame shows Zuikaku beyond Kaga).

ships.name: Hiei
ships.unit: Support Force / Battleship Division 3, 1st Section (flagship of VAdm Mikawa Gunichi)
ships.funnels: Two upright funnels; tall pagoda foremast of the prototype tower type later used for Yamato.
ships.note: Carried Type 95 (E8N) reconnaissance floatplanes used for local patrol.

formation.basis: E: schematic. Fuchida (S) puts the two battleships and two heavy cruisers on the outer flanks of the carrier columns; which flank and how far is not known to me.

formation.description: Launch disposition ('No. 6 alert cruising disposition', assumed at 00:30 JST = 05:00 HST per Genda). Attested: six carriers in two parallel columns of three; two battleships and two heavy cruisers on the outer flanks; light cruiser and destroyers as a screen around the force; three submarines far ahead; tankers astern during the crossing (Fuchida 1952). Reconstructed here: starboard column Akagi-Kaga-Zuikaku, port column Soryu-Hiryu-Shokaku, 7,000 m between columns and between ships in column; Abukuma 10 km ahead on the centreline; Tone/Chikuma on the forward flanks and Hiei/Kirishima on the after flanks about 8 km outside the columns; seven destroyers on a loose ring (Arare and Kasumi were away with the tankers).
formation.offsetConvention: ships[].formation.rightM / aheadM are metres from Akagi measured in the frame of the BASE course 180 deg (aheadM positive = south, rightM positive = starboard = west). The turns into the wind were made by all ships together, so while launching each ship heads about 070 deg but keeps the same earth-frame offsets: rotate headings, not the pattern.
formation.transitFormation: During the crossing (No. 1 cruising disposition) the same two columns of three were kept much closer together, on the order of 1,000-1,500 m between ships (the film frame from Akagi shows Kaga and Zuikaku close astern), with the seven tankers astern, the battleships and heavy cruisers outboard and the three submarines scouting ahead.
formation.planeGuard: IJN practice was to station a destroyer 700-1,000 m astern of each carrier during flight operations to pick up ditched crews (a Zero pilot who crashed on take-off in the first wave was rescued by a destroyer). Which destroyer followed which carrier is not known to me; an animation may move the ring destroyers astern of the carriers during the two launches.
formation.basis: S: Fuchida, 'I Led the Air Attack on Pearl Harbor' (two columns of three, flank and screen description, tankers astern, submarines about 200 miles ahead); S: Genda memoir excerpt (disposition No. 6 at 00:30 JST); S: NHHC caption of the film frame from Akagi; S: Japanese forum pointer that the No. 5 and No. 6 dispositions are drawn in Senshi Sosho vol. 10 (not accessible). E: column sides, the 7,000 m spacing (the First Air Fleet's 1941-42 box-formation doctrine as described in Evans & Peattie and Parshall & Tully, recalled, not re-verified) and every escort station.

plan.source: Carrier Striking Task Force Operations Orders No. 1 and No. 3 of 23 November 1941 as reconstructed after the war in Japanese Monograph No. 97 (S). The originals were destroyed; the text was rebuilt from notes and memory.

standbyPoint.note: JM-97 prints 42 N 165 W; the 1946 Joint Committee narrative prints '42 north, 170 east' (an obvious slip for west); Wallin has 'longitude about 170 W, then course about 135'. 170 W adopted.

approachPoint.note: JM-97. Turn south at about 24 knots from its vicinity around 07:00 JST on X-1 day (11:30 HST 6 December).

plan.order3: 700 nm due north of point Z at 06:00 JST X-1; course 180 at 24 kn from 07:00; first wave launched 230 nm due north of point Z at 01:30 JST (06:00 HST); second wave 200 nm due north at 02:45 JST (07:15 HST); then withdraw northward at about 24 kn; first wave due back 05:30-06:00 JST (10:00-10:30 HST), second 06:45-07:15 JST (11:15-11:45 HST).

pointZ.note: JM-97 defines point Z as the western extremity of Lanai. Taken literally the first launch would be at 24.75 N 157.06 W, only about 190 nm from Kahuku Point bearing 016 deg. That does not fit the Opana radar track (first wave came in from 3 deg east of north), so the actual launch is placed near 158 W.

plan.order1Variant: Order No. 1 version: take-off point 200 nm north of the enemy anchorage at 01:00 JST X-day (05:30 HST).

dec7.event: All ships turn together to port into the wind (01:20 JST); carriers hold 24 knots. Battle ensign and 'Z' flag at Akagi's masthead.

launchPointAnalysis.radarCrossCheck: Opana first plotted the wave at 07:02, 132-137 statute miles (115-119 nm) out, 3 deg east of north, and lost it about 20 statute miles out at 07:39 (about 157-165 kn ground speed). A wave leaving 25.45 N 157.86 W at 06:20 covers the 111 nm to the 07:02 plot at 159 kn. A launch at 26 N would need about 200 kn; a launch north of Lanai would put the 07:02 bearing near 019 deg instead of 003.

deckProcedure.spotting: Each deck load was ranged aft with wings spread in take-off order: fighters at the front of the pack (shortest run), then the B5N level bombers or D3A dive bombers, with the torpedo-armed B5Ns last at the stern (longest run). Aircraft were armed and fuelled in the hangars, brought up by the lifts from about 03:30 and warmed up on deck. The second deck load was struck below ready and brought up as soon as the first wave had gone.
deckProcedure.signals: Air officer on the bridge orders the launch; the deck launch officer released each aircraft with a white hand flag, at night a green lamp swung in a circle (Fuchida). Chocks pulled, deck crews held the wingtips against the roll and waved caps as each aircraft passed. A steam jet at the bow showed the relative wind. Akagi flew the 'Z' flag with the battle ensign.
deckProcedure.lighting: Dark: launch began in nautical twilight about 35 minutes before sunrise at the force's position (sunrise there about 06:35; Honolulu 06:26). Waning gibbous moon (about 84 percent lit) in the western sky behind broken cloud. Dim deck-edge and centreline lights; aircraft showed navigation and formation lights to join up, and the leaders signalled by lamp.
deckProcedure.formUp: After take-off aircraft turned left and climbed in a wide left-hand orbit around the force, units joining on their leaders, made one circuit and set off south over the flagship at about 06:20. Cruise order of the first wave: Fuchida's 49 level bombers leading at about 3,000 m; 40 torpedo planes to the right and slightly below (about 2,800 m); 51 dive bombers to the left and above (about 3,400 m); 43 fighters above as cover (about 4,300 m). The wave flew above a cloud layer with tops near 2,000 m.

wave1.leader: Cdr. Fuchida Mitsuo (observer in Akagi B5N2 AI-301, pilot Lt. Matsuzaki Mitsuo)

order.note: LtCdr. Itaya Shigeru, fighter leader; first off the deck.
LtCdr. Hashiguchi Takashi. 15 planned; one failed to launch.
LtCdr. Takahashi Kakuichi, dive-bomber leader. 27 planned.

wave1.intervalBasis: E: 183 aircraft from six decks in about 15 minutes; Akagi's 36 aircraft imply about 25 s between take-offs. Fighters can go at 10-15 s, loaded B5Ns nearer 30 s.
wave1.abortsNote: S: Arakaki & Kuborn - one horizontal bomber, three dive bombers and two Zeros failed to launch, all for mechanical trouble before take-off. S: NPS - one Zero crashed into the sea on take-off (pilot picked up by a destroyer) and another was left aboard with engine trouble. Attribution to carriers is by arithmetic (planned minus launched) and is M/E; which carrier's Zero crashed is not established here.
wave1.note: Sequence within each carrier (fighters, then level or dive bombers, then torpedo planes) is M (Prange, Fuchida), medium confidence. Launch start is 06:00 in Japanese records; 06:05, 06:10 (NPS timeline) and 06:18 (combinedfleet) also appear, and one timeline says Nagumo held the launch briefly for the sea state.

order.note: Lt. Shindo Saburo, second-wave fighter leader.
LtCdr. Egusa Takashige, dive-bomber leader. 18 planned; one turned back with engine trouble.

wave2.note: S: 54 B5N, 78 D3A, 35 A6M = 167. The four shortfalls against the plan of 171 are assigned to carriers by arithmetic (M/E). Japanese chronologies time the launch 02:45 JST = 07:15; NPS has the carriers turning into the wind at 07:05; one Japanese site gives 07:45. Arrived off Kahuku Point about 08:40 and was ordered to attack at 08:54 (S: Fuchida).

cap.schedule: Standing patrols rotated about every two hours from an hour before sunrise until 45 minutes after sunset (S: Wallin). The first patrol went up with the first wave; mainly Shokaku and Zuikaku fighters.
cap.floatplanes: Besides the two 05:30 scouts, floatplanes from the battleships and cruisers flew close anti-submarine and search patrols around the force (M, details not verified).
cap.note: 39 fighters for combat air patrol is S (USNI Proceedings 1991: 432 aircraft = 353 raid + 39 CAP + 40 reserve). Wallin (S) says 54. The per-carrier split is E: fighter complement minus the fighters assigned to the two strikes.

recovery.returnRendezvous: Aircraft left Oahu via an assembly point 20 nm from Kaena Point on bearing 340 deg, fighters joining bombers for navigation, then flew north to the carriers.
recovery.note: Times are M (Prange, standard accounts) and only approximately known; the position is E. Landing in a heavy swell wrecked a number of damaged aircraft, which were pushed overboard. Loss totals by carrier: S (combinedfleet TROMs for Akagi and Soryu) and M for the rest.

thirdStrikeDecision.who: VAdm Nagumo on the advice of his chief of staff RAdm Kusaka ('We should retire as planned').
thirdStrikeDecision.advocates: Fuchida's post-war account has him urging another attack on returning, with Genda in support, and RAdm Yamaguchi (CarDiv 2) signalling that Soryu and Hiryu were ready. Aircraft were in fact being rearmed and ranged when the decision was made. Parshall and Zimm argue that Fuchida's bridge scene is embellished or invented and that a strike on fuel tanks and yards was not on anyone's agenda that afternoon.
reasons: Mission judged accomplished after two waves
US carriers unlocated; only about ten floatplanes available to search
Losses rose sharply in the second wave as defences woke up
A third strike would land after dark in a rising sea
Fuel: tankers already sent to the rendezvous, destroyers short-legged
Within range of land-based bombers thought to survive on Oahu

withdrawal.note: Direction reported as north or north-north-west; value is E.

thirdStrikeDecision.aftermath: Yamamoto's staff aboard Nagato urged ordering another attack; Yamamoto left the decision to the man on the spot. On 16 December (JST) Soryu, Hiryu, Tone, Chikuma, Tanikaze and Urakaze were detached to support the second Wake Island attack; the rest reached Hashirajima on 23-24 December.

scoutPlanes.type: Aichi E13A1 Type 0 reconnaissance seaplane ('Jake'), three crew
scoutPlanes.crew: Sources differ: Japanese Wikipedia names WO Fukuoka Masaharu; Pacific Wrecks names the pilot as Ito Akira.

route.note: Estimated landfall north of Oahu, above the cloud deck. Opana logged small plots north of Oahu at 06:45-06:51 that are usually put down to the scouts.
Observing Pearl Harbor through cloud breaks; position schematic.
Then searched south of Oahu for carriers without result (Pacific Wrecks); schematic.

reports.text: Enemy fleet at anchor in Pearl Harbor: nine battleships, one heavy cruiser, six light cruisers. (Prange's wording, recalled. Fuchida's 1952 article gives ten battleships, one heavy cruiser, ten light cruisers.)
Wind direction 080 degrees, speed 14 metres per second; cloud over the enemy fleet at 1,700 metres, amount 7. (Japanese Wikipedia times the Chikuma plane's report 03:08 JST = 07:38.)

scoutPlanes.note: Route is a dead-reckoned schematic; only the launch time, target and the content of the reports are attested. The reports were the first radio transmissions from the force since leaving Japan.

scoutPlanes.type: Aichi E13A1 Type 0 reconnaissance seaplane ('Jake'), three crew
scoutPlanes.crew: Pilot WO Narukawa Ryozo (combinedfleet, Pacific Wrecks).

route.note: Dead reckoning, course about 165 deg, 289 nm to run.
Dead reckoning; passes east of Oahu and north of Molokai.
Lahaina Roads in sight between Maui, Lanai and Molokai; anchorage empty.

reports.text: The enemy fleet is not in Lahaina anchorage. (Another account times this about 07:40.)

scoutPlanes.note: Route is a dead-reckoned schematic. Reaching Lahaina by 07:35 needs about 140 kn over the ground, which the E13A could manage with the north-easterly wind on its quarter. Submarine I-72 had already reported Lahaina empty on 6 December.

submarines.organisation: Sixth Fleet (Advance Expeditionary Force), VAdm Shimizu Mitsumi in the cruiser Katori at Kwajalein. Special Attack Unit of five Type C1 boats each carrying one Type A midget (Capt. Sasaki Hankyu in I-22). Submarine Squadrons 1, 2 and 3 formed the cordon around Oahu; I-10 and I-26 reconnoitred the South Pacific and Aleutians. With the three boats attached to the carriers, 30 fleet submarines took part.

typeA.armament: two 45-cm Type 97 torpedoes in superimposed bow tubes; 140-kg scuttling charge
typeA.enduranceNote: about 80 nm at 6 kn, under an hour at full speed; battery only, no means of recharging

mothers.name: I-16

launch.basis: S: combinedfleet - 7 miles SSW of the harbour entrance. Coordinates computed from the harbour mouth (21.317, -157.967).

mothers.note: First to launch. Received radio messages from her midget at 22:41 on 7 December and 00:51 on 8 December.

mothers.name: I-22

launch.basis: S: combinedfleet - 9 miles from the entrance (arrived at the launch point 01:10). Bearing not given; due south assumed.

mothers.note: Flagship of the Special Attack Unit (Capt. Sasaki Hankyu).

launch.basis: S: combinedfleet - about 13 miles from the entrance. Bearing not given; south-south-east assumed because her midget ended up off Keehi Lagoon, east of the entrance.
S: combinedfleet - 5.3 miles from the entrance. Bearing not given; assumed.

mothers.name: I-24

launch.basis: S: combinedfleet - 10.5 miles WSW of the entrance.

mothers.note: Last to launch; the midget's gyrocompass was known to be defective.

motherRecoveryRendezvous.note: Mother boats were to wait about 7 nm west-south-west of Lanai on the nights of 7-8 and 8-9 December; no midget arrived. E: coordinates from that description (M).

crew: PO2c Ueda Sadamu (also read Uyeda Tei)

track.event: Launched 7 nm SSW of the harbour entrance.
I-16 receives a radio message from the midget reporting the air attack a success. Position unknown; one theory has the boat hiding in West Loch.
Last message: unable to navigate.

midgets.fate: Lost; no survivors. Both torpedoes had been fired. The hull, cut into three sections, lies in a military dumping ground about 3 nm south of Pearl Harbor among debris from the 1944 West Loch disaster; the sections were located by the Hawaii Undersea Research Laboratory in 1992, 2000 and 2001 and the identification announced in 2009. Whether it got into the harbour and fired at Battleship Row (a much-argued photograph), or fired at the cruiser St. Louis off the entrance at 10:04, is not settled.

wreck.basis: E: 'about three miles south of Pearl Harbor'; exact position not published in anything reached.

track.event: Launched 9 nm off the entrance.
Estimated: passes the anti-torpedo net, whose gate stood open from 04:58 until about 08:40, and works up the channel submerged.
Conning tower sighted by USS Zane about 200 yd astern of Medusa, north-west of Ford Island; then by Curtiss, Medusa and others.

Fires a torpedo at Curtiss (misses, explodes against a dock at Pearl City); Curtiss puts a 5-inch shell through the conning tower. Second torpedo fired at the charging Monaghan misses and explodes on the Ford Island shore.
Rammed by USS Monaghan, then blown to the surface and sunk by two depth charges in about 9 m of water.

midgets.fate: Sunk in the harbour west-north-west of Ford Island at 08:43-08:44; both crew killed. Raised later in December and used, with the crew's remains inside, as fill for a quay at the submarine base. Identified as Iwasa's boat from a lieutenant's shoulder insignia (he was the only lieutenant among the ten).

wreck.basis: E: placed from the Curtiss/Medusa berths (X-22 and X-23 as recalled; one source prints K-23 for Medusa) and the Ford Island shoreline; not a surveyed position.

track.event: Launched about 13 nm off the entrance.
Depth-charged and abandoned off Keehi Lagoon, east of the harbour entrance; time unknown.

midgets.fate: Found by US Navy divers on 13 June 1960 in about 23 m (75 ft) of water off Keehi Lagoon with depth-charge damage, both torpedoes still in their tubes, the hatch unclipped from inside and no remains. Raised, returned to Japan and displayed at the former Naval Academy, Etajima.

wreck.basis: E: 'off Keehi Lagoon in 75 ft'; original find position not located.

track.event: Launched 5.3 nm off the entrance.
Seen from USS Antares following her and her towed lighter toward the entrance, conning tower awash.
Sighted by USS Ward; general quarters 06:40.

Ward opens fire at about 100 yd: first shot misses, second (No. 3 gun) holes the base of the conning tower on the starboard side; four depth charges as Ward passes over. A PBY of VP-14 (Ens. Tanner) adds depth bombs. Ward reports at 06:53.

midgets.fate: Sunk by USS Ward at 06:45, the first shots of the Pacific War; both crew lost. Wreck found on 28 August 2002 by the University of Hawaii's submersibles Pisces IV and V in about 400 m of water roughly five statute miles off the harbour mouth, sitting upright with the shell hole in the conning tower and both torpedoes aboard. That this was I-20's boat is the usual attribution, not a certainty.

wreck.basis: E: HURL gives 400 m depth about five miles off the mouth of Pearl Harbor (press reports say three to four miles); coordinates are not published. Placed due south of the harbour mouth at that distance.

crew: Ens. Sakamaki Kazuo (captured, first Japanese prisoner of war)

track.event: Launched 10.5 nm WSW of the entrance with a dead gyrocompass; broaches, trim corrected.
Estimated: nearing the entrance, running on periscope and magnetic compass.
Runs onto a reef beside the entrance channel and surfaces.
USS Helm, leaving harbour, fires on the stranded boat and misses; the boat slides off and submerges. A second grounding wrecks the torpedo gear; depth-charging and battery fumes disable the crew.
Estimated: drifting east past Diamond Head, out of control.
Strands on the reef off Waimanalo Beach near Bellows Field. Scuttling charge lit but fails; crew go into the surf.
Sakamaki, washed ashore, is captured by Cpl. David Akui of the 298th Infantry. Inagaki's body comes ashore later.

midgets.fate: Never fired a torpedo. Grounded off Bellows Field, salvaged intact by the Army, toured the United States on war-bond drives and is now at the National Museum of the Pacific War, Fredericksburg, Texas.

wreck.basis: E: reef a few hundred metres off the Bellows/Waimanalo beach; not a surveyed position. Times on 8 December are approximate.

relatedContacts.event: Minesweeper Condor sights a periscope about 1.75 nm south of the entrance buoys and signals Ward at 03:57. Which midget is unknown.
Cruiser St. Louis, clearing the channel, reports two torpedoes exploding on the reef near entrance buoy No. 1 and fires at a conning tower. Possibly I-16's boat; disputed.

TROM: 'north of Oahu'.
Next to I-25.
Easternmost boat of the line.
Flagship of the boats stationed north of Oahu.
Westernmost section of the Kauai Channel.
Kauai Channel, between I-1 and I-3.
Easternmost section of the Kauai Channel, off Kaena Point.
Off the north-east coast of Oahu (Makapuu), next to I-6.
Northern entrance of the Kaiwi (Molokai) Channel, between I-4 and I-5.
North of Molokai.
TROM as summarised places her north-west of Oahu, unlike the rest of the squadron; uncertain.
25-50 miles south-west of Oahu; ordered with I-69 to lie off the entrance to rescue midget crews.
25-50 miles south-west of Oahu; later fouled a net off Barbers Point.
About 10 miles off the entrance to Pearl Harbor. Sunk by Enterprise aircraft north-east of Oahu on 10 December.
Off the entrance between I-70 and I-73. Had scouted Lahaina Roads on 6 December and reported it empty.
Off the entrance, east of I-72.
25-50 miles south-east of Oahu.
25-50 miles south-west of Oahu.
South of Niihau as lifeguard for aircraft told to ditch there.
About 110 miles north-east of Oahu during the air attack.
North of Oahu, between the island and the carriers; nominal position only.
With the carrier force until reassigned at 15:10; nominal position only.
About 1,000 nm north-east of Oahu; sank the freighter Cynthia Olson at about the hour of the attack. Position M.
Returning from scouting Fiji and Samoa, far south of Hawaii; the TROM summary says 'south of Oahu'. No position given.

submarines.cordonNote: All cordon coordinates are E: the station descriptions in the combinedfleet TROMs (S) turned into nominal points. They show which sector each boat watched, nothing finer.

weatherAtLaunch.seaState: Rough: long heavy swell from the north-east, carriers pitching hard with spray over the forward flight decks; rolls of 11 to 15 degrees reported.
weatherAtLaunch.cloud: Broken to overcast, base roughly 1,000-1,500 m, tops near 2,000 m; the first wave flew above it at 3,000 m. Over Oahu at 07:38: wind 080 deg at 14 m/s, cloud at 1,700 m, amount 7.
weatherAtLaunch.moon: Waning gibbous, about 84 percent illuminated (full moon 3 December), in the western sky.
weatherAtLaunch.note: S: a Japanese chronology gives 'ENE wind 13 m/s' at 06:00 with the carriers working up to 24 kn into it; Jiji says the decks tilted as much as 15 degrees; Fuchida says the sea was rough, the wind strong and the sky dark, and calls the wind 'northerly'; English accounts say 'east' (one says a 10-knot east wind). Twilight and moon values are E (computed).

aftermath.note: Midway Neutralization Unit (Ushio, Sazanami) shells Midway that night.
I-70 sunk north-east of Oahu by SBDs from USS Enterprise.
JST: Soryu, Hiryu, Tone, Chikuma, Tanikaze and Urakaze detached for Wake Island.
JST: main body anchors at Hashirajima (23-24 December).
